$description: Pi Pocket's own design system: Tokyo Night in dark, a light day mode, and a high-contrast mode.

com.pi-pocket.name: Pi Pocket
com.pi-pocket.description: The look of Pi Pocket: soft tiles over a Tokyo Night palette, Geist for words, JetBrains Mono for code.

150.$description: A half step, kept on purpose: the light mode's sunken well must be a shade darker than the canvas (100) and still hold muted text at 4.5:1, and 200 is too dark for that.

550.$description: A half step, kept on purpose: the one gray that reaches 3:1 on a light ground and on a dark one, so a field border and a switch track use it in every mode.

750.$description: A half step, kept on purpose: the dark mode needs a ground between surface (800) and selected (700) for what is raised.

neutral.$description: Blue-gray neutrals, light to dark. Regular steps of 100 from 0 to 700, then of 50 to 950: a dark interface needs its grounds (850 base, 800 surface, 750 raised, 700 selected) closer together than a light one.

blue.$description: The accent. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own blue.

red.$description: Errors and danger. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own red.

yellow.$description: Warnings. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own yellow.

orange.$description: The brand mark. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own orange.

green.$description: Success. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own green.

cyan.$description: Information and code operators. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own cyan.

magenta.$description: Thinking and keywords. A regular ramp: lightness falls at each step. 400 is Tokyo Night's own magenta.

alpha.$description: Overlays: the text color laid over a ground at a few percent, as the app does for hover, press, and hairlines.

scrim-dark.$description: Dim layer behind sheets, on dark grounds.

scrim-light.$description: Dim layer behind sheets, on light grounds.

canvas.$description: The desk behind everything. In high contrast, canvas, base, and sunken are one black: edges separate them, not tints.

surface.$description: Cards and panels on the ground.

raised.$description: Controls and anything lifted off a surface. In light mode it is the same white as surface: the shadow lifts it.

selected.$description: A selected row or segment: an accent tint in light mode, a lifted gray in dark and high contrast.

sunken.$description: Inset areas: code blocks and wells. A shade darker than the canvas in light mode; in high contrast it is the canvas black, and an edge sets it off.

hover.$description: Overlay on a hovered row or button.

pressed.$description: Overlay on a pressed row or button.

scrim.$description: The dim layer behind a sheet.

primary.$description: Headings and the words that matter.

muted.$description: Hints, timestamps, and secondary labels. Reads at 4.5:1 on every ground, a selected row too. In high contrast it is the same color as secondary, because it needs 7:1 there.

inverse.$description: Text on a strong, neutral fill.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls only. WCAG exempts disabled text from contrast, so it is below 4.5:1 on purpose: never use it for words that matter or for a placeholder.

subtle.$description: A hairline between tiles and rows.

default.$description: A visible line: cards and dividers.

strong.$description: The edge of a field or a switch track. Reaches 3:1 on every ground.

default.$description: Links, icons, and accents on a ground.

fill.$description: The fill of a primary button.

soft.$description: A quiet accent wash behind selected things.

line.$description: The border of an accent wash.

default.$description: Errors and destructive actions. Text and icons.

line.$description: The border of a danger message.

fill.$description: The fill of a destructive button.

fill-hover.$description: The destructive fill under the pointer.

default.$description: Warnings and cautions. Text and icons.

line.$description: The border of a warning message.

default.$description: Success and done. Text and icons.

line.$description: The border of a success message.

default.$description: Information and neutral notices. Text and icons.

line.$description: The border of an info message.

bg.$description: The ground of code: the same as the sunken well.

text.$description: Code without a color of its own.

mono.$description: Code, paths, branches, numbers, counts, and keys. Ligatures off, as in a terminal.

size.$description: The type scale, close to 1.125 above 14 px.

duration.$description: Hyprland's speeds, rounded to six steps.

z.$description: Stacking order of layers over the page.

space.$description: The spacing scale, on a 4 px grid: the steps that padding, margins, and gaps use, which a design reads as they are. Nothing else is in this group: roles that use a step are in layout, and a component keeps its own.

radius.$description: Corners. A scale of five steps and round, and the roles that point at it: a role says what it rounds, and the value comes from the scale. Three roles are 1 or 2 px off the app's own corners, so that the scale has no step of its own for them (see each).

scale.$description: The steps. Every corner of the system is one of these.

xs.$description: State squares and the smallest marks.

sm.$description: Inline code, keys, tags, and segments.

xl.$description: Sheets, the message box, and pop-ups.

seg.$description: A segment in its track. The app uses 5 px; here 4 px, on the scale.

control.$description: Icon buttons, fields, segmented tracks. The app uses 7 px; here 6 px, on the scale.

window.$description: Windows, approval cards, peek tiles. The app uses 10 px; here 8 px, the same as a card.

sheet.$description: The message box, sheets, the launcher.

float.$description: Pop-ups and menus. The same step as a sheet; kept apart so that floating things can be rounded on their own.

tap.$description: The smallest touch target on a touch screen.

size.$description: Sizes of controls, icons, and avatars (heights and widths), not spacing: used as they are. A component keeps the sizes that are its own.

breakpoint.$description: Minimum widths. Below md is the phone layout.

shadow.$description: Soft lifts. The shadow color follows the mode.

lift.$description: A soft lift: the message box.

float.$description: What floats over the page: pop-ups, sheets, the launcher.

hairline.$description: A 1 px outline drawn as a shadow, so layout does not move.

focus-ring.$description: The keyboard focus ring: a soft halo around a solid line. Keep it visible.

type.$description: Text styles. Each is one family, size, weight, line height, and tracking.

display.$description: Page titles and the home screen.

title.$description: A screen or a sheet title.

in-out.$description: Things that move across the screen.

focus-offset.$description: The gap between a button and its focus ring.

gap.$description: The gap between segments, and around them.

padding-y.$description: The vertical padding of a badge.

dot.$description: The status dot in a badge.

notice.$description: A message that sits in the page.

menu.$description: Rows in a pop-up menu or a list.

padding.$description: The padding of a menu around its rows.

step.$description: A step in an activity timeline.

layout.$description: The gaps of Pi Pocket's tiled layout.
